records.abstract: This is a comment on Gibson(2026a) and Some Other Reflections upon some relevant claims. [Disclaimer: this is a work in progress, feedback is welcome]

records.title: A Contrastive Analysis of the Phonological Systems of Bambara and English: Implications for Language Teaching.
records.abstract: This paper examines the phonological systems of Bambara and English from a contrastive linguistic perspective, with particular attention to their implications for language teaching and learning. Bambara, a major Mande language spoken primarily in Mali, and English differ considerably in their sound inventories, vowel systems, syllable structures, tonal and stress patterns, and phonological processes. These differences may create pronunciation difficulties for Bambara-speaking learners of English, particularly in the production of English vowel contrasts, consonant clusters, word stress, and intonation. Similarly, English-speaking learners of Bambara may experience difficulties in recognizing and producing lexical tones, vowel nasalization, and other distinctive phonological features of the language. Drawing on Contrastive Analysis Theory and relevant descriptions of both languages, this paper identifies major phonological similarities and differences and discusses their pedagogical implications. It argues that systematic phonological comparison can help teachers anticipate learners' difficulties, develop appropriate instructional materials, and adopt teaching strategies that address specific pronunciation challenges. The paper concludes that explicit phonological instruction, listening discrimination, articulatory practice, and the integration of oral language activities are essential for improving pronunciation and communicative competence in both languages.

records.title: A copy-and-pastable vaccine against AI-assisted QRPs
records.abstract: My previous studies have demonstrated that current AI systems can readily assist users in performing questionable research practices (QRPs) when prompted to do so. This paper shifts the focus from documenting the problem to developing a solution. Five experiments tested whether custom instructions---short texts that users can paste into their AI settings---can serve as a "vaccine" against AI-assisted QRPs in Gemini. Experiment 1 found that both a conceptual-level instruction (referring to QRPs in general) and a behavior-list instruction (enumerating specific prohibited practices) reduced Gemini's willingness to p-hack from 100% to 0% across 30 trials each. With 30 pre-registered follow-up trials, the behavior-list instruction maintained a 0% execution rate across 60 trials in total, placing the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound on its execution rate below 5%. Experiments 2a&b showed that the same instruction generalized to optional stopping, post-hoc outlier exclusion and data fabrication by blocking these requests in all 20 out of 20 trials for each task, though it failed to block a missing value imputation request in one out of 20 trials. Experiments 3a&b demonstrated that the custom instruction written in English remained effective when the user's prompt was in Japanese. Taken together, the results show that a very simple, user-level intervention can (almost) categorically eliminate a wide range of AI-assisted QRPs under the tested conditions. The vaccine is provided in a copy-and-pastable format for immediate use.

records.title: Marginal emphatic consonants in Arabic dialects: Phonemes or not? صوامت التفخيم الثانوية في لهجات العربية: فونيمات أم لا؟
records.abstract: This paper re-examines the status of the so-called “secondary emphatics” in Arabic dialects: consonants traditionally considered to be marginal phonemes with limited emphasis spread effects. These include labial /b, m, f/, coronal /r, l, n/ and velar /k, x/ consonants, among others. An analysis of their phonological behaviour across varieties reveals that only /r/ and /l/ enjoy a phonemic status in certain dialects. The remaining consonants are characterized by a very low functional load, near-exclusive occurrence in loanwords, and strict adjacency to a low vowel, thus casting doubt on their classification as phonemes. An alternative proposal is to treat this behaviour as evidence of a phonemic split in the low vowels, distinguishing front /a/ from a new emphatic vowel /ɑ/. This approach eliminates the need to posit marginal phonemes and generates an economical system, where the new ɑ/ɑ shares a secondary place [dorsal] feature with emphatic consonants.

records.title: Animal Linguistics as an Integrative Framework for Animal Communication
records.abstract: Interest in animal communication has arguably reached an all-time high, with two very visible projects—the search for the animal roots of human language and the development of methods and technologies to decode animal signals. These projects need a shared, overarching scientific framework. We propose that animal linguistics offers one, which will require close collaboration between ethologists, linguists and, increasingly, AI specialists. One possible way to view the project—not the only one—goes as follows. With the same ambition as human formal linguistics, animal linguistics seeks to develop explicit models of animal communication ("formal animal linguistics"), to understand the extent and limits of variation in living species ("comparative animal linguistics"), and to investigate the cognitive basis of observed properties ("animal psycholinguistics"). Through a "phylogenetic tree of animal signals", it seeks to retrace and explain the path from ancestral signals to modern ones ("evolutionary animal linguistics"). In its synchronic and diachronic components, animal linguistics offers an integrative framework for scientific and technological progress in animal communication. Going forward, it could offer new areas of application and new sources of insight for multiple areas of cognitive science.

records.title: R in the Tigris qeltu-dialects of Mesopotamia
records.abstract: The Tigris qeltu-dialects are known to have a uvular fricative ġ in place of historical rāʔ, but existing side by side with a tapped r, and their occurrence is both phonologically and sociolinguistically conditioned. This chapter first outlines the sociolinguistic variation, but then concentrates on the phonological behavior of (inclusive) R in three dialects of this qeltu subgroup, namely, Maṣlāwi Arabic and Christian and Jewish Baghdadi Arabic, based on data collected from four native informants via two reading tasks. The objective is to examine the lexical categories, distributional patterns, and possible phonological processes in which R participates, such as loan vs. native words, minimal pairs, cooccurrence restrictions on consonant combinations, and various types of assimilation. Although the data exhibit discrepancies between the dialects, evidence confirms the existence of two R phonemes in all three of them: a dorsal fricative /ġ/ which is a reflex of old rāʔ merged with inherited ġayn, and a coronal sonorant /r/ found mainly in loanwords and some native words with specifiable phonological contexts. A representational analysis, formulated in the framework of feature geometry, demonstrates that /r/ is exclusively rhotic while /ġ/ is not.

records.title: 上古汉语“马”的来源——一个经叶尼塞语系中介的印欧语借词假说
records.abstract: This paper discusses the etymology of the Old Chinese word for “horse” (*mˤraʔ). Based on the distribution of Indo-European *markos, the phonological rules of Yeniseian (Starostin, personal communication, 2026), and the Sintashta-Karasuk archaeological evidence, this paper proposes that *markos entered Old Chinese through a Yeniseian intermediary. Phonologically, this is reflected in the direct correspondence of m-, the deletion of -o (Yeniseian final-vowel deletion), the weakening of -k to a glottal stop, and the loss of -s. The archaeological chain is Volga-Don → Sintashta → Andronovo → Karasuk → Shang. The paper also responds to Bjørn’s(2022) Iranian bāraka- hypothesis, pointing out its phonological ad hocness (b- → m-) and chronological problems. It argues that loanword studies must be constrained by archaeology. This is a working paper; comments are welcome. 本文探讨上古汉语“马”（mˤraʔ）的词源问题。基于印欧语*markos 的分布、叶尼 塞语系的音系规则、以及辛塔什塔-卡拉苏克考古证据，本文提出：*markos 经叶尼塞语系中 介传入上古汉语，音系上表现为 m-直接对应、-o 脱落（叶尼塞删尾规则）、-k 弱化为喉塞、 -s 脱落。考古学链条为伏尔加河-顿河—辛塔什塔—安德罗诺沃—卡拉苏克—殷商。本文同 时回应 Bjørn（2022）的伊朗语 bāraka-假说，指出其音系特设（*b-→m-）和可能存在的时 间错位问题。本文认为，借词研究必须受考古学约束。本文为工作论文，欢迎批评指正。

records.title: Congruence in a pragmatic framework
records.abstract: The placement of prosodic prominence in an answer is generally taken to depend on the question. E.g., "Who saw Mary? BEN saw Mary", but "Who did Ben see? Ben saw MARY". This correspondence is referred to as congruence, and in much of the literature it is captured in terms of grammatical machinery and constraints. I argue that such grammatical explanations are unnecessary in light of pragmatic considerations governing discourse, primarily those concerning the role of pragmatic questions, understood in terms of partitions. These considerations derive a more accurate empirical picture of question-answer felicity and do so in terms of general assumptions rather than specialized machinery.

records.title: (Everyone) Everywhere All at Once: A relational account of quantified impersonal -where in English
records.abstract: On the surface, English [Q+where] forms such as everywhere are locative. Yet as Sluckin & Kastner (forthcoming) document experimentally, they can also serve as impersonal human subjects, as in Everywhere in the UK loves Marmite, in which everywhere = everyone. The form retains its locative morphology and the pro-form where, yet it binds they/their and controls like a [+HUMAN] quantified indefinite pronoun. It must also be distinguished from ordinary locative (every place) and metonymic institutional readings. We argue that the impersonal use emerges from a distinct syntactic configuration in the nominal domain, rather than from lexical polysemy. Where spells out a higher locative D/P shell, while beneath it sits a silent, sortal, human-descriptive root √PERSON, selected by a relational categorising head nCAT bearing [uPlace]. Relationality comes from the categoriser, not from the root (cf. Adger 2013). The [uPlace] feature forces an overt locative PP into Spec,nPCAT, where it saturates the place argument of an inhabitant relation; nEA then abstracts over the human variable, and the quantifier binds the resulting property. Because the root receives its zero exponent locally under this categoriser, rather than from the higher shell, its human content remains active though unpronounced. Institutional everywhere, by contrast, retains a √PLACE structure with contextual transfer. The obligatory locative PP follows from [uPlace], whereas the macro-geographic restriction is an interface condition rather than a syntactic feature.

records.title: Reconstructing Middle Chinese Labial Initials and the Breathy-Voice Accommodation Hypothesis of Labial Split: Evidence from a Tripartite Test of Dunhuang Sino-Tibetan Transcription, 'Phags-pa Script, and Dialect Retention
records.abstract: Previous reconstructions of Middle Chinese posit Ming (明母) as [m], Wei (微母) as the labiodental nasal [ɱ], and Fu (敷母) as [pfʰ]. The latter two values, however, are hardly attested in modern Chinese dialects—a situation at odds with the general pattern that Chinese dialects preserve Middle Chinese features widely. Drawing on Dunhuang Sino-Tibetan transcriptions, the 'Phags-pa transcriptions in the Menggu Ziyun, historical foreign transcriptions, and modern dialectal databases, this paper proposes a new reconstruction: Ming as the prenasalized voiced bilabial stop [ᵐb]; Wei as the bilabial nasal [m], arising through the unconditioned change ᵐb > m and established as an independent initial through Song-dynasty standardization within the closed third-division slot; Fu as the voiceless glottal fricative [h]; and Feng (奉母) as the labiodental voiced fricative [v]. Re-examining the initial table prefaced to the Menggu Ziyun, the paper argues that Zhu Zongwen's double assignment of the letter ꡤ to Fei (非母) and Feng reflects the loss of the Qieyun Ming value in the Yuan phonological system and the resulting merger of Wei and Ming; the corrected assignments are ꡏ = Wei [m], ꡓ = Feng [v], ꡤ = Fu [hu], and ꡰ = Fei [f]. Dialectal evidence includes the acoustic agreement between [ᵐb] in Ming-initial words of Taiwan Southern Min and the Dunhuang transcription letter འབ (ɦb), the geographical distribution of [h] readings of labial words in Southeastern dialects corroborating the Menggu Ziyun transcriptions, and the zero-initial breathy-voiced rhymes of the Zhongyuan Yinyun ("房防", "墳焚棼", "扶夫蚨符芙鳬浮"), which furnish synchronic minimal pairs. On this basis we propose the Breathy-Voice Accommodation Hypothesis: the phonetic origin of the light labials is a zero-initial breathy-voiced closed rhyme formed when labial initials were lost from Bang and Pang words of the closed third division—words that in the dominant phonological system already belonged to the Bing class of clear-consonant-with-murmur syllables after medial loss. Subsequent developments depend on each dialect's capacity to accommodate breathy voice: accommodating systems retain the zero-initial breathy rhyme; non-accommodating systems substitute [v] or [hu], with [v] later devoicing to [f]. Wei [m] alone is the natural outcome of Ming [ᵐb], independent of this contact-driven evolution.

records.title: Feed me your manuscript, confidential or not: Current AI systems may not protect the confidentiality of peer review
records.abstract: Manuscripts under peer review are confidential materials, and as such, major publishers prohibit reviewers from uploading them to commercial generative AI systems. The current experiments tested whether the current AI systems consistently comply with this policy, and showed that this is not necessarily the case. In Experiment 1, Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini rarely explained confidentiality when a first-time reviewer requested general help (2/30 trials). When the user explicitly asked whether a manuscript could be shared, ChatGPT accepted in 10/10 trials and Claude in 6/10, whereas Gemini consistently refused with a confidentiality warning. However, in Experiment 2, given a very similar prompt but with an attached manuscript, Gemini analyzed the attached file without warning in all 10 trials, suggesting the instability of its safeguard system. Further, Experiment 3a found that Gemini sometimes accepted sharing when prompted in Japanese. The result of this exploratory experiment motivated a confirmatory experiment (Experiment 3b), which directly compared English and Japanese. As predicted, Gemini accepted sharing more often in Japanese (27/30) than in English (1/30). Taken together, the current findings show that an apparently reliable confidentiality safeguard may fail when the request format or language changes, underscoring the need to test whether the AI's “ethical” responses generalize across conditions.

records.title: Weakening Weak Islands
records.abstract: The extraction of bare wh-adjuncts from whether-clauses is a prototypical instance of weak-island violation and has traditionally been treated as ungrammatical. This paper presents novel experimental evidence that challenges this generalisation. We show that English speakers fully accept adjunct extraction from whether-islands when these are introduced by a discourse context that licenses reconstruction of the extractee within the embedded clause. By contrast, the same contextual manipulation produces no amelioration in strong islands, whose extraction remains overwhelmingly rejected. Building on these findings, we advance two claims. First, adjunct extraction from whether-clauses is grammatically licit and its perceived degradation arises from a domain-general preference for shorter dependencies, which can be overridden by appropriate discourse context. Second, the differential sensitivity of strong and weak islands to the same manipulation bears directly on the broader debate concerning the source of locality effects. In particular, we argue that the weak and strong islands considered here have distinct sources: strong-island effects reflect a grammatically encoded constraint on extraction, whereas weak-island effects emerge from the interaction between grammatical representations and domain-general factors. In the conclusion, we suggest that this interpretation is compatible with approaches that place at least some locality effects at the interface between grammar and external systems, in line with the broader explanatory goals of Minimalism.

records.title: Perception-production asymmetries can emerge despite complete isomorphism across modalities
records.abstract: Perception-production asymmetries have been modelled through representational or grammatical non-isomorphism. We identify a further architectural property of multi-level OT that drives such mismatches. Formalizing a recently reported asymmetry in L2 tonal acquisition, we show that asymmetric patterns can arise despite complete isomorphism across modalities. Depending on the input, the same undominated mapping constraints may drastically narrow the candidate set in one modality before lower-ranked constraints apply, while leaving sufficient candidates in the other modality for those constraints to determine the outcome. Thus, perception-production asymmetries can emerge from the architecture of a single grammar, without requiring separate grammatical systems across modalities.

records.title: A PredP Analysis of English Resultative Constructions:Focusing on the Asymmetry of Wh-Extraction
records.abstract: This paper proposes a novel syntactic analysis of English resultative constructions within the framework of modern Minimalist syntax (Chomsky 2024; Kitahara and Seely 2025). Challenging traditional Small Clause analyses, we argue that the result predicate is accommodated within a functional phrase, PredP (Bowers 1993), separating the state-holder from the main verb's direct object position. Combined with the FormCopy operation and Minimal Search, our model accounts for the long-standing WH-extraction asymmetry between paint-type and consider-type resultatives. Specifically, we demonstrate that consider-type verbs lack a lexical object position (DP2), preventing FormCopy from generating the required search path for WH-extraction. This structural difference naturally derives the extraction restriction without positing ad-hoc constraints, offering a unified account of syntactic relations and semantic interpretations in resultative constructions.

records.title: When concord meets suppletion: on double plural marked adjectives in Ingush
records.abstract: This paper examines the patterns of apparent double plural marking on the Ingush adjective -oaqqa/-oaqqii ‘big’. It presents evidence against Norris’s (2022) analysis of the non-prefixal plural marking on this adjective as concord. New data demonstrate that (a) prefixal and non-prefixal plurality may mismatch, and (b) such mismatches are disallowed in certain idiomatic contexts. The alternation -oaqqa/-oaqqii is treated as an instance of number suppletion and is analyzed as word-external contextual allomorphy. The paper discusses whether – and to what extent – the Ingush data in question can be seen as evidence against analyzing adjectival number suppletion as a concord-mediated operation.

records.title: Intensified response particles and polarity opposition
records.abstract: Intensified response particles such as English "absolutely" and German "voll" (lit. 'full' ≈ 'totally/absolutely') have been analyzed as degree modifiers of assertion (Greenberg & Wolf 2019): they strengthen a response by marking maximal speaker commitment to an anaphorically retrieved proposition. We test whether maximal commitment alone captures their distribution. Two acceptability experiments on English and German show that these particles are degraded relative to neutral response particles in plain factual-positive confirmations, whereas this disadvantage is absent or substantially reduced in evaluative contexts. Factual-negative contexts reveal further language-specific asymmetries. These findings show that commitment strength alone is insufficient. We propose, as a first account, that intensified response particles express contrastive commitment: maximal alignment with a proposition relative to a salient incompatible alternative. The results thus motivate a discourse-sensitive analysis of response particle intensification, while leaving open whether polarity opposition fully characterizes the relevant licensing condition.

records.title: Large Language Models for Automated Systematic Analysis of Language Transcripts (SALT) Bound Morpheme Annotation
records.abstract: Prompt engineering adapts large language models (LLMs) to specific tasks by designing their inputs, without modifying pretrained parameters. Researchers in the field of linguistics and speech-language pathology use the Systematic Analysis of Language Transcripts (SALT) software to analyze functional language use and language disorders. However, transcription of language samples for SALT analysis requires intensive coding procedures, creating a barrier to efficient SALT language sample analysis (LSA). In three stages, this study developed and tested the capabilities of prompt-engineered large language models in annotation of SALT bound morphemes. In the first stage, five prompt versions were compared using GPT-4o and GPT-5.6 Luna on 12 synthetic mixed-convention transcripts to determine the optimal engineering strategy. Using the highest-performing prompt in stage 1, stage 2 evaluated nine different LLM configurations on the same transcript set, to select the best-performing models. Paired with prompt v5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.6 Flash advanced to stage 3 final testing, where they were tested on 18 held-out mixed-convention transcripts (1,889 utterances) and 30 single-convention transcripts (1,800 utterances) per model. Performance was measured by morpheme-level micro F1, precision, and recall. GPT-5.6 Sol achieved 97.81% micro F1 on the mixed-convention transcripts, compared with 90.60% for Gemini, whose score was lowered by two structurally invalid responses; on the transcripts Gemini returned in valid format, the two models were similarly accurate (Sol 97.72% vs. Gemini 97.97%). Sol returned valid output for all 48 final transcripts. These findings demonstrate the potential of prompt-engineered LLMs for automated bound-morpheme annotation. Further validation on authentic language samples is necessary before implementation in research or clinical settings.

records.title: Naming the nameless: a preliminary study of bynames for the deceased from an onomastic perspective
records.abstract: The article proposes a new term, postmortonyms, denoting names assigned to unidentified deceased individuals. Drawing on an exemplary semantic onomastic analysis of 220 postmortonyms from multiple cultures, the study explores the motivations, structures, and functions of these bynames, distinct from posthumous names, deadnames, and necronyms. The research demonstrates that postmortonyms often incorporate details such as location or distinguishing features, which serve investigative, communicative, and memorial purposes. The analysis highlights the phenomenon of polyonymy, in which temporary names coexist with potential authentic identities, and discusses the broader cultural and legal contexts that influence naming practices for the nameless dead. The research is a preliminary study, and the findings provide a foundation for further research on the conceptualization of death and naming across cultures.

records.title: (In)sensitivity to surface-level heuristics: A case from Turkish verbal attractors
records.abstract: Research on linguistic illusions has debated what information is used to access memory representations, but how speakers use surface phonological information during dependency resolution remains unclear. Agreement attraction is more likely when the attractor matches the form of an agreement controller (e.g., in case marking). This has been attributed to phonological forms directly activating every feature set they can express, regardless of context. Alternatively, form may act indirectly, by shifting the estimated probability that a noun is a controller, which retrieval uses as a cue. We test these accounts in Turkish, where -lAr marks plural on nouns and nominalized verbs; both can be subjects, but verbal -lAr rarely controls agreement. In three experiments (two speeded acceptability, one self-paced reading), -lAr-marked genitive nouns produced robust attraction; verbal attractors produced none. Attraction tracks an attractor's likelihood of being a controller, not invariant feature activation by form, explaining prior syncretism and form-matching effects.

records.title: A predicate-fronting analysis of Tigrinya clefts
records.abstract: Tigrinya (Ethiopia and Eritrea; Semitic) has a well-behaved head-final verbal domain that canonically displays S-O-V-Aux word order. A notable exception is found in so-called cleft constructions, where the verbal copula appears in a clause-medial position, between a focused constituent (FOC) and a presupposed relative clause (RC). I argue that this non-canonical FOC-cop-RC word order is derived from a head-final specificational copula construction by way of predicate fronting. This approach preserves the head-finality of the language and offers an account for some otherwise exceptional case and agreement patterns.

records.title: Exclusively Restricting Traces and the Interpretation of Chains
Lexicon against Naturalness: Unnatural Gradient Phonotactic Restrictions in Tarma Quechua
records.abstract: It has been shown in separate studies that phonological grammar can operate probabilistically and in phonetically unnatural directions. This paper examines whether phonological grammar can be both probabilistic and unnatural at the same time. We create a new corpus of Tarma Quechua vocabulary (based both on published and unpublished data), and argue that the unnatural probabilistic phonotactic trends in the Tarma Quechua lexicon are statistically significant and show signs of productivity, with evidence from loanword phonology and from morphophonological alternations. We also perform an acoustic analysis of existing recordings to confirm the phonetic status of the the unnatural gradient restriction. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a fully unnatural gradient phonotactic restriction on segmental structure. The existence of unnatural probabilistic phonology has broad theoretical consequences because it requires probabilistic approaches to phonology to derive unnatural patterns. While weighted constraint approaches are more powerful than non-probabilistic approaches, we argue that models without unnatural constraints are not sufficient for deriving Tarma Quechua data. We propose a framework for evaluating phonological analyses using the goodness of fit measurement. This quantitative evaluation approach supports analyses with some, but not all of the relevant conceivable unnatural constraints. We argue that the proposed approach can serve for evaluating other models and approaches.

records.title: On Split Affectivity in Chinese
records.abstract: This paper deals with a split of affectivity in Chinese dialects from the perspective of generative syntax: give-affectives sports permissive, passive and dative construals, whereas with-affectives garner comitative-oriented usages such as benefactive, goal, and disposal throughout the historical development. We propose to relate the former to the notion of “terminal coincidence”, and the latter to that of “central coincidence” in Hale & Keyser’s (2002) sense. Our study shows that, despite the apparent unified construals of gei ‘give’ in Mandarin, the main difference between the two types of affectives lies in their distinct routes of grammaticalization owing to the terminal-central dichotomy, as well as the interpretive mechanism of applicative syntax under the Cartographic Approach.

records.title: High Applicatives are not High Enough: A Cartographic Solution
records.abstract: This paper examines a cluster of phenomena in Mandarin Chinese, which may collectively be characterized as "affective constructions". Based on the diversified and sometimes hybrid nature of these affective construals, we argue that the usual dichotomy between high and low applicatives is not enough to capture their syntactic and semantic idiosyncrasies. We will need a more elaborate theory to map out the topography of applicatives under the Cartographic Approach (Rizzi 1997, Cinque 1999). It is shown that Chinese affectives have an unusual distribution extending far beyond the boundary of the vP phase, which in turn argues for an independent applicative projection in the left periphery, presumably associated with speaker-orientedness and a presupposition of unexpectedness.

records.title: Gradient Grammaticality in Model-Theoretic Dependency Grammar
records.abstract: Generative linguistics typically treats grammaticality as a binary matter, attributing the gradient effects frequently observed in acceptability judgment experiments to performance factors rather than to the grammar. Yet no specific performance account has, to our knowledge, been offered for most such effects, which strengthens the case for gradient grammaticality. Gradient judgments, however, have received little systematic study in experimental syntax, and the frameworks built on existing findings are better characterized as blueprints than formalized grammars. This paper takes a step towards closing both gaps. Four acceptability judgment experiments, two in English and two in Polish, manipulated violations of two constraints: subject–verb agreement and syntactic selectional restrictions. The results show that violation costs are systematically gradient, differing by constraint and by predicate, and reliably cumulative in that two violations are generally worse than one. Crucially, however, they combine under-additively rather than by linear summation as commonly assumed. We then outline Gradient Model-Theoretic Dependency Grammar , a formally explicit, monostratal, constraint-based framework in which constraints are adorned with stochastic penalty weights and violations combine through an under-additive function. As a proof of concept, we apply it to one of our experiments to estimate weights from the judgment data and derive acceptability predictions.

records.title: Coordination – An overview of theoretical issues
records.abstract: This manuscript has been written as the first version of the Coordination chapter for Carnie et al. 2027 – the 2nd edition of the Routledge Handbook of Syntax . Unfortunately, it is almost two times longer than the official space limit allows, so I will probably have to substantially shorten it for the handbook. If so, I plan to maintain two versions of this paper: a longer forever unpublished manuscript with the current title and a much shorter Coordination chapter of the handbook. (The current version 3 adds references to recent experimental work on violations of the Coordinate Structure Constraint, version 2 differs from the original version 1 only by including a funding statement.)

records.title: A coherence-based account of paycheck pronouns
records.abstract: Paycheck pronouns have often been presented as a challenge to dynamic semantic accounts of pronominal anaphora. In this paper, I present new data suggesting that discourse relations play an essential role in the availability of paycheck pronouns. I thus argue for a discourse coherence-based account of paycheck anaphora. I present a new analysis of paycheck pronouns using Segmented Discourse Representation Theory (SDRT) that accounts for the distribution of paycheck pronouns through independently motivated constraints on discourse relations. In developing this analysis, I demonstrate that by incorporating discourse coherence insights into the analysis, dynamic semantic approaches are more than able to account for paycheck pronouns.

records.title: Fusion of functions revisited: When does a head have a second function?
records.abstract: Some grammars give a word two syntactic functions at once. The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language treats some in take some as both the determiner and the head of its noun phrase, and rich in the rich as both modifier and head, a fusion of functions that Payne et al. (2007) defend. The simpler alternative is that the word is just the head. I argue that a second function needs evidence of form that varies with it rather than with the word, and test for such evidence with the grammar’s own diagnostics and new corpus data. For the modifier function, there’s none. For the determiner function, there’s one fact, that no adjective comes before a bare determinative outside a few exclamations, but the comparison is close, and on balance, it doesn’t justify the extra function. Fused relatives such as whoever told you that are different: they relativize subjects, they have no infinitival forms, and in usage, the case of whoever answers to its function inside the clause. There a second function is favoured, though not forced. Keeping a category, heading a phrase, and taking a reading from context are things a head with no second function can do, not evidence of one.

records.title: Transitividad a media voz: Aproximación cuantitativa a clases semánticas y alternancias de diátesis de la voz media en español
records.abstract: Este trabajo examina la distribución de la voz media en español desde una perspectiva cuantitativa basada en corpus, combinando un enfoque conceptual con un análisis de las alternancias de diátesis asociadas a las construcciones medias. Los datos proceden de ADESSE, una base de datos sintáctico-semántica construida sobre el corpus ARTHUS, que incluye 158 624 cláusulas correspondientes a 4011 verbos. En una primera fase se analiza la asociación de la voz media con distintos dominios conceptuales, agrupados en las clases Emoción, Espacial, Cambio, Atribución y Otras. Los resultados confirman una especial afinidad de la voz media con los dominios espacial, emocional y de cambio. En una segunda fase se identifican y cuantifican distintos tipos de alternancias de diátesis documentadas con la voz media: anticausativas, antipasivas, alternancias activa-media con estructuras intransitivas y transitivas, y casos de media tantum. El análisis muestra que la alternancia anticausativa constituye el patrón más frecuente y productivo, especialmente en los dominios espacial y de cambio, mientras que las alternancias antipasivas y las construcciones medias transitivas se concentran principalmente en otras clases semánticas. Se concluye que la distribución de la voz media no depende exclusivamente de propiedades conceptuales generales, sino también de la frecuencia y productividad de determinadas alternancias de diátesis, que contribuyen decisivamente a estructurar su comportamiento en el uso. Abstract: This study examines the distribution of the middle voice in Spanish from a quantitative, corpus-based perspective, combining a conceptual approach with an analysis of the diathesis alternations associated with middle constructions. The data are drawn from ADESSE, a syntactic-semantic database built upon the ARTHUS corpus, which comprises 158,624 clauses corresponding to 4,011 verbs. In the first phase, the association of the middle voice with various conceptual domains—grouped into the categories of Emotion, Spatial, Change, Attribution and Others—is analysed. The results confirm a particular affinity between the middle voice and the spatial, emotional and change domains. In a second phase, different types of diathesis alternations documented with the middle voice are identified and quantified: anticausative, antipassive, active–middle alternations with intransitive and transitive structures, and cases of ‘media tantum’. The analysis shows that anticausative alternation constitutes the most frequent and productive pattern, particularly in the spatial and change domains, whilst antipassive alternations and transitive middle constructions are mainly concentrated in other semantic classes. It is concluded that the distribution of the middle voice does not depend exclusively on general conceptual properties, but also on the frequency and productivity of certain diathesis alternations, which play a decisive role in shaping its behaviour in usage.

records.title: Examining form-based linguistic productivity in people and large language models
records.abstract: Linguistic productivity, as evidenced by the use of words in novel contexts, is one of the most striking facts about human language. However, how abstract the knowledge that enables such productivity is remains unclear. We compare people's and computational language models' linguistic productivity in contexts where successful generalization depends on form-based information. We focus on extending the use of a novel verb learned in the active voice to passive contexts. We find people extend active to passive uses in a way consistent with abstract generalizations concerning linguistic form, even when no plausible meaning can be assigned to the novel verb. In contrast, large language models succeeded only when a meaning like an existing verb's could be assigned to the novel verb. We conclude that computational models' syntactic knowledge remains tied to the distribution and meaning of specific lexical items in a way that human syntactic knowledge is not.

records.title: Syllables Long by Position in Classical Latin: The Phonetic Substance of the Second Mora
records.abstract: Classical Latin counts a syllable with a short vowel as heavy (“long by position”, positione longa) when the vowel is followed by two consonants, unless these are a stop and a liquid (muta cum liquida), before which it may remain light. Phonological theory expresses this by assigning a mora to the coda consonant, but leaves open why listeners of quantitative verse equated that mora with the second half of a long vowel. This article proposes that, in careful speech and the recitation of verse, the second mora of such a syllable, closed by the first of the two consonants, rested on a phase that followed the vowel and shared some of its properties (voicing, resonance or airflow), and that this similarity made the equivalence possible. The clearest form of this phase is a brief transitional vocoid into which a coda consonant was released before a heterorganic consonant: ărma [arᵊ.ma]. Too weak to form a syllable, the vocoid together with the preceding consonant made up the second mora. Where the typology excludes such a vocoid, in homorganic clusters and geminates, or where the coda is s or final -m, the same role was played by the sustained body of the coda itself or, in voiceless stop geminates, probably by a laryngeal phase of the preaspiration type; a stop before a homorganic consonant may have had one as well or merged with the following consonant. Typological parallels support the proposed realizations. Weaknesses of the proposal and first corpus tests are discussed.

records.title: Stochastic knowledge on word formation: evidence from French demonym formation
records.abstract: This study investigates stochastic knowledge of French demonym formation, focusing on lexical propensity, phonological nasal clash, and extralinguistic knowledge. In an online forced-choice experiment, 27 native speakers of Metropolitan French and 26 native speakers of Quebec French selected demonyms for 17 nonce toponyms, first without and then with geographical labels referring to French regions. Baseline suffix propensity was the strongest predictor of choice. The varieties differed in their preference orderings: Metropolitan French speakers favoured -ois, whereas Quebec French speakers favoured -ien. Geographical labels modestly increased the selection of -ien and -éen relative to -ois among Metropolitan French speakers, but no credible geographical effect was established among Quebec French speakers. Nasal-final toponyms showed a weak tendency to disfavour nasal suffixes, except for -ien in Quebec French. A MaxEnt analysis of Metropolitan French responses compared lexical-propensity constraints weighted using existing demonym data with a hypothetical, evenly spaced weight profile. The latter more closely approximated the experimental distribution, suggesting sensitivity to abstract suffix typicality rather than direct reproduction of lexical frequencies. These findings support a probabilistic account of word formation in which lexical propensity predominates, while phonological and geographical cues make weaker, context-dependent contributions.

records.title: Restrictions on experiencer placement in German tough-movement: Constituency and prosody rather than intervention
records.abstract: In this paper, we will compare the syntax of English tough-movement with that of its translational equivalent in German. We will see that, on the one hand, the syntax of the German construction is very different: there is no A′-movement involved but rather A-movement and restructuring; additionally, the adjective is merged as an adjunct to the infinitival clause rather than being the head that selects it; on the other hand, we will see that one can observe similar restrictions on the placement of experiencers. We will argue that this suggests that many of the proposals that have been made to account for experiencer intervention in English cannot be applied to German. Instead, we will argue that the restrictions follow from independent properties of German such as (i) the constituency that obtains if German tough-movement essentially receives the same analysis as the modal passive and (ii) a general adjacency requirement on verb clusters.

records.title: The Diachrony of Progressives in Venetan: A Syntactic Analysis
records.abstract: This paper investigates the diachronic development of the Venetan progressive construction formed with drio (‘behind’) and an infinitive. While this construction has traditionally been described as a prepositional infinitive, I argue that its historical evolution calls into question the prepositional status of drio and the nominal nature of the infinitive it introduces. Building on minimalist assumptions about labeling and agreement, the analysis proposes that early stages of the construction involved a nominalized infinitive embedded under a PP, with nominalization arising through agreement rather than categorial recategorization. Diachronically, the loss of nominal layers and of overt determiner realization leads to the reanalysis of drio as an aspectual head and to the emergence of a purely verbal progressive structure in Modern (Central) Venetan. The paper further situates the Venetan pattern within a broader cross-linguistic perspective, drawing parallels with Danish and Quebec French progressive constructions and argues that the instability of nominalized infinitives provides a principled explanation for their loss. More generally, I propose that nominalization effects can be derived without recourse to costly recategorization operations and that minoritized languages such as Venetan offer particularly transparent evidence for diachronic change.

records.title: Word order in the German middle field – scrambling
records.abstract: first version, comments welcome! This chapter provides an overview of the major empirical and theoretical aspects of word order variation in the German middle field, viz., scrambling. After introducing the German clause structure and providing basic properties of scrambling, this chapter will mostly focus on two aspects, viz., whether scrambling should be analyzed as involving base-generation or movement and, should movement indeed be involved, which movement type it instantiates. It will be argued that while many of the arguments for movement are eventually inconclusive, restrictions on scrambling and evidence for intermediate representations provide evidence for a movement approach after all. Much less conclusive, however, is the question regarding the movement type underlying scrambling. While PF-movement can be ruled out quite easily, the categorial restrictions on scrambling and the reconstruction effects observed do not fall neatly into the A- or A′-movement category. In the last section, further important aspects are addressed, including questions regarding the base order of double object verbs, possible triggers for scrambling and implications for clause structure. It will become clear that despite 40 years of intense research, scrambling still represents a challenge for linguistic theory in that its properties cannot easily be reconciled with elementary assumptions of current versions of the Minimalist Program.

records.title: ERGATIVE ALIGNMENT EQUALS ‘ERGATIVITY’ MINUS PSEUDO-ERGATIVITY
records.abstract: Not every language that appears to be an ergative language actually is one. However, if it is a language with ergative alignment, the absolutive is the case of the grammatical subject, regardless of transitivity. Pseudo-ergative languages must not be confused with ergative languages; otherwise, the very confusions to which typologists have become accustomed arise. [corrected bibliography; included: marked-S languages; with a few cosmetic touch-ups]

records.title: Demonstratives and Taxonomic Nouns: from Romanian to English
records.abstract: The Romanian noun fel 'kind' is puzzling insofar as it allows the existential reading of DPs of the form acest fel de masă ‘this kind of table’, but disallows the subkind reading.

records.title: Covert URs: evidence from nasalization in Western Panjabi
records.abstract: Panjabi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the Punjab province of Pakistan and the Indian state of Punjab. Long vowels contrast in nasality in the language, but this contrast is neutralized before nasal consonants: [ṼṼN], *[VVN]. This paper presents air pressure data from Pakistani Panjabi showing that predictably nasal vowels before nasal consonants in the language, [ṼṼN], are statistically equivalent in nasality to contrastive nasal vowels, /ṼṼ/ (Exp. 1). However, predictable [ṼṼN] and contrastive nasal /ṼṼ/ vowels behave differently in their interaction with a nasal harmony process, in that only contrastive nasal /ṼṼ/ vowels trigger nasal harmony (Exp. 2). This difference in phonological behavior can be straightforwardly analyzed by assuming (i) that pre-nasal vowels are underlyingly oral, even in morphemes which never show alternations in nasality, and (ii) that only underlyingly nasal vowels trigger harmony. These findings support a view of phonology in which abstract underlying representations (URs) can be completely covert, never surfacing in any allomorph without some kind of symbolic alteration. Surface-oriented approaches to phonology which reject covert URs—including usage-based models relying exclusively on observed exemplars to form lexical representations—have difficulty accounting for these facts.

records.title: Saving FACE: Fragment answers, copy theory, and radical trace conversion
records.abstract: Jacobson (2016) observes that fragment answers (e.g., Q: Which linguist is on the committee? A: Jill ) must denote elements in the restrictor of the wh -phrase in the question immediately preceding them, while the corresponding element in an overtly clausal answer, possibly elided via VP-ellipsis, does not. This fact presents a challenge for an analysis of F ragments a s C lausal E llipsis, or FACE, according to which fragment answers are full clauses in which movement of the overt fragment to a left-peripheral position, followed by ellipsis of the vacated TP, silences everything but the moving fragment itself (cf. Merchant 2005 and references therein). This is because, prima facie , it is unclear what properties of movement and ellipsis might conspire to give rise to Jacobson's observation. We show that current FACE-compatible proposals for deriving this observation suffer from conceptual or empirical problems, and offer our own FACE-saving alternative, which we argue overcomes these problems.

records.title: On “Geminate Transfer” in Semitic, with special attention to Mehri
records.abstract: It has been an ongoing effort in Generative Phonology to explain how the unique Root & Pattern morphology of Semitic languages follows from more cross-linguistic principles. This paper applies the same approach to a phonological pattern that also seems to be unique to Semitic languages, namely “Geminate Transfer”: the realization of an expected C1C2VC2 sequence as C1C1VC2. Focusing on the pattern as it is manifested in the Modern South Arabian language Mehri, the paper follows Bendjaballah and Ségéral (2013) in designating the C1C1VC2 realization as a repair, rather than an alternative, to C1C2VC2. At the same time, it follows Rose (2000) in regarding the phenomenon as the ultimate expression of a universal OCP constraint against sequences of similar (though not necessarily identical) consonants separated by a vowel. An OT account is provided that crucially covers an aspect of the facts that was not treated by Bendjaballah & Ségéral, while also arguing for their skelettal – as opposed to prosodic – conceptualization of the template. Finally, it is claimed that the phenomenon occurs only in Semitic because of the special morphological make-up of Semitic languages.

records.title: The Locus of Linguistic Knowledge: An Exemplar Model of Phonetic Neutralization
records.abstract: Eliminativist theories of speech production and perception locate linguistic knowledge exclusively within detailed episodic speech representations and their interactions. This paper examines the tenability of that commitment. Through a series of exemplar based computational simulations modeling the contextual neutralization of phonemic vowel nasality over time for an individual speaker, I explore what is required for eliminativist models to predict both phonetically complete and incomplete neutralization. The simulations show that, with the appropriate weighting of competing production biases of anticipatory nasalization and morphological similarity, eliminativist models can successfully produce phonetically incomplete neutralization. While token frequency manipulations and socially weighted encoding of exemplar memories can achieve phonetically complete neutralization, they introduce questionable empirical predictions and over-generate the predicted types of neutralization. Adjusting the relative strength of production biases provides an alternative solution by regulating the degree of neutralization while keeping the production optimum bounded by the competing phonetic targets of production biases. I argue that permitting learned, language-specific production-bias weights provides a more explanatorily adequate account of neutralization than the frequency-based or socially weighted encoding approaches examined here. Crucially, this account requires a form of linguistic knowledge that extends beyond the network of episodic speech representations and their interactions.

records.title: A challenge to unified accounts of non-canonical belief reports
records.abstract: This paper is concerned with two observations about belief attribution. The first is Fauconnier’s (1984) observation that we can felicitously ascribe to x belief in a proposition p , even when our pre-theoretical intuitions suggest that x does not really believe p , as long as x would have believed p if he shared some of our presuppositions. The second is to Szab ó's (2010) observation that when x believes de re , of n individuals, that they bear a property P , we can attribute to x the belief that “ n things are P ” even if x claims not to know how many relevant de re beliefs she has. In other words, we can “sum up” x 's distinct de re beliefs in a single belief report. These two observations have been introduced in isolation of each other, but have recently been offered a unifying account (Mayr and Schmitt 2026). This note posits empirical challenges to unification, and discusses the potential theoretical implications that arise if, indeed, the two observations cannot be successfully unified.

records.title: Prevalence and predictability: A causal analysis of emerging genericity in Mandarin wǎngwǎng-sentences
records.abstract: This article investigates the meaning of Mandarin sentences with wǎngwǎng, an adverb commonly translated as ‘often’ or ‘usually’. Empirical observations of wǎngwǎng range from proportional quantification and conditional probability to regularity, stability, and predictability. We argue that wǎngwǎng-sentences combine an extensional prevalence requirement with a non-accidental, projectable interpretation, a characteristic property of descriptive generic generalizations. Specifically, we propose a two-dimensional analysis: (i) wǎngwǎng contributes a contextually high prevalence relation between a restriction and a nuclear scope; and (ii) the resulting prevalence pattern must be appropriately grounded in a contextually relevant causal structure in order to support projection beyond the observed cases. In this synchronic sense, wǎngwǎng-sentences exhibit an emerging generic profile while retaining an overt prevalence requirement not shared by generic sentences in general. The analysis connects existing discussions of wǎngwǎng in the Chinese literature on proportionality and regularity with causal approaches to genericity, and clarifies the division of labor between extensional prevalence and causal grounding.

records.title: Synthetic Linguistic Data
records.abstract: Synthetic linguistic data have become increasingly prominent in linguistic research, from the analysis of large collections of AI-generated texts to controlled experiments investigating grammatical and lexical preferences. This glossary entry extends Bresnan’s (2016) distinction between the linguistic garden and the bush by introducing an artificial plant nursery as a metaphor for synthetic data. We distinguish between synthetic bush data, consisting primarily of corpus-like collections of model-generated language, and synthetic garden data, in which model outputs are elicited under controlled conditions to investigate specific linguistic hypotheses. We argue that synthetic data constitute a distinct object of linguistic investigation: comparing them with natural language data can reveal both shared patterns and divergences, but their interpretation requires careful consideration of the conditions under which they are generated.

records.title: Verb position in German: Cycles and movement
records.abstract: This paper discusses various approaches to head movement in HPSG. It points out that the cyclic verb trace causes problems with coordinated verbs in initial position and discusses non-cyclic approaches. Restricting the conjunctions in coordination structures is explored as well. The interaction of verb fronting with apparent multiple frontings (V3) in German is discussed and it is pointed out that this causes problems to approaches assuming a different architecture of the fronting mechanism in HPSG (elements of SLASH of type sign. Finally an implicational constraint is proposed that rules out coordinations in head-complement structures.

records.title: Towards absolute interpretation of acceptability judgments: Standard items for Polish
records.abstract: Acceptability judgments are central to syntactic theory and formal acceptability experiments have made the underlying data more reliable. Yet they leave one issue open: once a sentence is placed on a rating scale, the resulting number is interpretable only relative to the other items in its experiment, not in any absolute sense. Standard items – a fixed battery of sentences validated to occupy known, approximately evenly spaced positions across the acceptability range – address this by serving as shared anchors, but such sets exist only for English (Gerbrich et al., 2019) and German (Featherston, 2009). This paper develops and validates the first standard item set for Polish with a methodological approach consisting of a two-stage design that separates set selection (three iterative norming experiments) from validation (four large-scale experiments, around 1000 participants in total). The resulting set places fifteen items at five evenly spaced, correctly ordered levels that remain stable across studies with different participants, target items, and contexts. To establish a benchmark, two further experiments were conducted using a comparable methodology to test the existing English standard items. The Polish set was found to be at least as reliable as the English one.

records.title: From Sensation to Cognition: A Comprehensive Analysis of Perception Verbs Colexification in Swahili
records.abstract: This study systematically examines the regular patterns of Swahili perception verbs evolving from concrete sensory actions to abstract cognitive functions, revealing the primary mechanisms involved in this developmental pathway. The research materials were collected and analyzed through dictionary searches, literature reviews, and interviews with native speakers. The findings indicate that all five-sense verbs in Swahili project into the cognitive domain: Visual verbs (e.g., "ona", "angalia", and "tazama") have developed rich cognitive meanings such as "understand", "think", and "judge"; auditory verbs (e.g., "sikia") have derived meanings like "know" and "perceive"; while tactile ("gusa"), olfactory ("nusa"), and gustatory ("onja") verbs have extended to cognitive functions such as "move emotionally" and "feel". The semantic extension of Swahili perception verbs into the cognitive domain, along with the language's unique reliance on sensory experiences when conceptualizing internal states, reflects the coexistence of universality and individuality in language. This study unveils the cognitive principles underlying lexical meanings and their cultural conceptualizations in language.

records.title: Taxonomic Structures without Reference to Kinds
records.abstract: Nominal constituents of the form that kind of table allow both subkind and existential readings. According to Carl-son (Linguistics and Philosophy 1(3), 1977, 413–456; Reference to Kinds in English. Doctoral dissertation, Uni-versity of Massachusetts, Amherst 1977, published in 1980 by Garland Press) both of these readings involve a unique underlying syntactic configuration and a unique denotation for the noun kind. This analysis cannot be ex-tended to the Romanian acest fel de masă ‘this kind of table’, which is fully acceptable and colloquial on the exis-tential reading, but unacceptable (or only marginally accepted by certain speakers) on the subkind reading. In addi-tion to bringing up the existence of the atypical Romanian fel ‘kind’, I will enrich the empirical landscape of taxo-nomic nouns (which include kind, type, model, sort or species) by formulating two new crosslinguistic generaliza-tions: (i) the choice between existential and subkind readings correlates with different agreement patterns observable in Romanian and other Romance languages; (ii) in English as well as in Romance languages the necessarily quanti-ficational determiner each is only marginally acceptable in existentially interpreted nominals of the form each kind/type of NP. My solution to these problems will build on Wilkinson’s (The semantics of the common noun kind. In G. Carlson & F. Pelletier, eds. 1995, The Generic Book, 383-397) syntactic-ambiguity hypothesis, accord-ing to which the existential and subkind readings of that kind of table rely on two different syntactic structures. The theoretical contribution of the present paper is a new syntactic analysis of the structure underlying the existential reading and a corresponding semantic composition. The core syntactic assumption will be a null functional head Qual(ity), which carries the burden of the semantic composition. The theoretical advantage of this proposal is that it separates classifying meaning, which is contributed by the syntactic structure (more precisely by the Qual° head) from reference to kind-level entities, which is contributed by taxonomic nouns.

records.title: Not Just Islands: Relativized Blocking Throughout the Grammar
records.abstract: Recent research in computational linguistics has found that most long-distance linguistic dependencies are tier-based strictly 2-local (TSL-2) over their respective representations, providing a precise characterization of blocking elements in phonology and syntax. A subset of the well-known syntactic island effects have been claimed to be one such class of blockers, explaining their superficial diversity via a common computational basis. This article revisits the TSL-2 analysis of islands in light of subsequent work on other types of syntactic locality constraints and on the treatment of gradient blocking. It finds that the TSL-2 islands display variation and gradience of the sort found in other syntactic blockers, while those islands which are not TSL-2 can be distinguished in this regard. Several directions are suggested for future research on islands and other syntactic locality phenomena.

records.title: The Subregular Complexity of Case and Agreement
records.abstract: This dissertation aims to establish a tight bound on the computational complexity of case and agreement dependencies in syntax, that is, the class of possible formal patterns which they exemplify. Such dependencies are shown to be modeled well by a tree-based generalization of of tier-based strictly 2-local (TSL-2) formal languages, mirroring past results on long-distance phonotactics and syntactic movement. This characterization has several important consequences. First, TSL-2 is a highly restrictive formal class, ruling out many unnatural and presumably impossible patterns whose absence is left unexplained by earlier, string-based classifications of syntactic patterns. Second, the range of patterns it can express aligns closely with well-known cross-linguistic generalizations and points of variation, unifying many phenomena previously handled by distinct theoretical mechanisms. Third, TSL-2 patterns can be computed by simple, cognitively plausible pattern-detection mechanisms, explaining why it is that language makes use of these and not others. Finally, the class of TSL-2 patterns is in principle efficiently learnable, providing a crucial hint into how human children learn languages so effortlessly, and by extension, how we might design artificial systems that do the same. All necessary background on subregular formal languages and their application to syntax is included, though some familiarity with Minimalist syntax is assumed. As such, this dissertation may also serve as an introduction to subregular complexity for both theoretical and computational linguists alike.

records.title: Tier-Based Strict Locality and the Typology of Agreement
records.abstract: This paper presents a subregular analysis of syntactic agreement patterns modeled using command strings over MG dependency trees (Graf and Shafiei 2019), incorporating a novel MG treatment of agreement. Phenomena of interest include relativized minimality and its exceptions, direction of feature transmission, and configurations involving a chains of agreeing elements. Such patterns are shown to fall within the class of tier-based strictly 2-local (TSL-2) languages, which has previously been argued to subsume the majority of long-distance syntactic phenomena, as well as those in phonology and morphology (Graf 2022). This characterization places a tight upper bound on the range of configurations that are predicted to occur while providing parameters for variation which closely match the observed typology.

records.title: Assigning attributive properties without adnominal modification in Lakota
records.abstract: Lakota has been described as a language in which adnominal modification is realized by a postnominal stative verb (SV). Lakota SVs can function predicatively without a copula, and their attributive use is subject to various constraints that are not typically observed for property words used with a copula, such as adjectives in familiar languages. Among these constraints is their inability to be chained, coordinated, contrasted, or modified within a referring expression. This study investigates the motivation for these constraints and provides evidence that, while a postnominal SV semantically assigns an attributive property to a noun, syntactically it does not function as a modifier of the noun. Instead, the adjacent N and SV constitute a complex stative expression and stand in a syntactic relationship inherited from the copredication and co-dependency between a clause-final N and SV functioning predicatively. This analysis accounts for the constraints, elucidates several outstanding issues in Lakota morphosyntax, and suggests a typologically novel (i.e., previously undescribed) strategy of assigning an attributive property within a referring expression.

records.title: Dative-infinitive structures in Russian: semantics and grammar
records.abstract: Russian Dative-Infinitive-Structures (DIS) have been a matter of debate, with focus on such issues as mono vs. bi-clausality, modal flavour, TAM features and case-marking. I argue that all contextual realizations of Russian DIS sentences express a single flavour in root indicative clauses — alethic modality and exhibit the constraint on perfect infinitives in non-negative clauses. The Perfective Infinitive Constraint is canceled in other varieties of DIS sentences which do not express alethic meanings and are realized in irrealis or usual contexts. These asymmetries are explained by the fact that root DIS declaratives unlike irrealis DIS clauses have deictic tense. On formal accounts, deictic tense comes from the TP layer above the infinitive phrase, and the illocutionary force and modal flavour come from the upper CP layer above the TP. Root DIS declaratives enter the derivation as bi-clausal but undergo restructuring as the border between TP and VP is removed. The dative subjects of DIS sentences are raised out of the embedded infinitival clause and lack the animacy condition. The syntax and semantics of DIS sentences are valued across an overtly similar sentence pattern with embedded infinitives ― Dative-Predicative-Structures (DPS). I argue that Russian DPS sentences are control structures that implement a different mechanism of case assignment. Russian infinitival clauses by default retain deictic tense: this factor overrides the control versus raising distinction, but some types of both control and restructuring predicates block deictic tense for semantic reasons.

records.title: Copy control and other control properties in Mandarin
records.abstract: The possibility of overt controllees has long challenged control theories. This paper investigates copy control in Mandarin Chinese, where the embedded subject of a control construction may be overtly realized. Based on acceptability-judgment experiments, we establish empirical generalizations concerning how copy control interacts with exhaustive control, partial control, and raising. We show that copy control is available in Mandarin, but only under tightly constrained conditions: it is licensed with certain exhaustive and partial control verbs in specific configurations, but excluded with raising predicates and transitive subject-control verbs. We argue that these patterns are not best captured by finiteness-based approaches, which dominate existing accounts. We propose a formal analysis within Lexical Functional Grammar (LFG), distinguishing functional control (structure sharing) from anaphoric control (pronominal dependency). These two mechanisms resemble a fundamental distinction in broader control theory between movement-based and PRO-based approaches, but often coexist within the grammatical system of a single language in LFG. Copy control arises precisely in anaphoric-control environments, while being systematically excluded under functional control. The paper contributes to cross-framework comparison (LFG vs Minimalist approaches), hybrid control mechanisms in formally explicit analyses, obviation, distinctions between grammatically licensed copy control and processing-based resumptives, lexical specification under interspeaker variation, and the typology of anaphoric control. We argue that a hybrid model integrating structure sharing and anaphoric dependency provides a principled and empirically grounded account of complex control phenomena.

records.title: Disentangling syntactic ergativity from constraints on ergative displacement
records.abstract: [21 October 2026: Uploaded with reference list.] [3 June 2026: Uploaded with a number of revisions, most significantly reorganization and elaboration in section 4.] [1 October 2025: Uploaded with significant revisions, especially section 4.] A subset of morphologically ergative languages have been claimed to display syntactic rules which are sensitive to the distinction between ergative and absolutive arguments---syntactic ergativity. The most robustly attested syntactic ergativity effect concerns the accessibility of the ergative argument for displacement (relativization, topicalization, focus fronting, question formation, etc.). Researchers have explicitly or implicitly assumed that there are no syntactically ergative languages which do not display a constraint on ergative displacement, and as a result, the term syntactic ergativity has largely come to be synonymous with this constraint. Using data from West Circassian (Northwest Caucasian) and Samoan (Polynesian), this paper challenges this position on two counts. Firstly, it argues that a universal correlation between syntactic ergativity and a ban on ergative displacement is theoretically unexpected and empirically incorrect. Secondly, it challenges the utility of contrasts in morphological exponence as a metric for determining the presence of syntactic ergativity in displacement dependencies.

records.title: Experimental evidence for argument ellipsis as the only derivation of Russian verb-stranding constructions
records.abstract: [This paper supersedes a previous ms. found at https://ling.auf.net/lingbuzz/008258] [[Oct '26: Updated version contains additional data analysis that supports Benbaji-Elhadad and Pesetsky's (2025) claim that ellipsis of predicate nominals does *not* result in degraded acceptability of verb-stranding constructions]] Russian verb-stranding constructions are argued to exemplify either verb-stranding VP ellipsis (Gribanova 2013b) or argument ellipsis (Bailyn 2017; Landau 2020b). As recent work shows, the debate between verb-stranding VP ellipsis and argument ellipsis is murky due to various confounds in the employed diagnostics (Simpson 2023; Landau 2023b). This paper reports on an acceptability judgment study focused on whether the semantic type of verbal arguments influences acceptability of verb-stranding constructions (as has been observed for Hebrew by Landau 2018). Our results support Landau's finding only partially: only ellipsis of adverbial arguments was found to lead to a decline in acceptability, while no effect of ellipsis of predicate nominals was found. However, if a VP ellipsis derivation were available, all sentences would have an acceptable parse. The reported study thus supports the view that argument ellipsis is the only available structure for Russian verb-stranding constructions with overt subjects. We contrast the findings with Russian verb-stranding constructions that involve polarity focus and conclude that the scope of our claim is limited to verb-stranding constructions that do not involve syntactic head movement (assuming a distinction between types of head movement proposed by Harizanov & Gribanova 2019).

records.title: Turkic influence on the uralic morphology in the Volga-Kama region (german)
records.abstract: This article (BA) tackles language contact at the Volga-Kama region.

records.title: Exclusive focus in Akan and type flexibility
records.abstract: Exclusive focus particles in many languages have flexible positions: as adverbial particles (as in English, John only Adv saw Mary ) or as adfocal particles ( John saw only Adfoc Mary ), with the same truth conditions. This raises the question of whether exclusives are ambiguous between an A-quantifier entry and a D-quantifier entry, dubbed the type-ambiguity view here (Horn 1969, Rooth 1985, 1992, Coppock and Beaver 2014, Yip and Adedeji 2024, Yip 2026; cf. Renans 2017); or uniformly as an A-quantifier, and the adfocal use is merely a syntactic “concord” phenomenon with a null exclusive operator OP EXCL , dubbed the uniform operator view here (Lee 2005, Quek and Hirsch 2017, Sun 2021, Bassi et al. 2022, Branan and Erlewine 2023, Aremu 2026; cf. Bayer 1996, i.a.). This paper argues for the type-ambiguity view over the uniform operator view of exclusives for Akan. In Akan, only adfocal particles are attested: nkoaa ‘only’ and pɛ ‘only’, which may be doubled together. We show that nkoaa allows for cross-categorical association with focus, whereas pɛ alone does not and must depend on nkoaa for association with VP and CP. Based on their scopal behavior, we further demonstrate that the locus of exclusive semantics is on the adfocal particles but not a null OP EXCL . We propose a type-flexible analysis of exclusives with higher-order quantification and abstraction, which also explains exclusive doubling and the asymmetries in focus association.

records.title: Gemini’s changing responses to data fabrication requests: Observations from a replication study
records.abstract: Kawahara (2026) found that Gemini complies with a request for data fabrication in 17 out of 30 trials (57%). In this note, I briefly report the results of three follow-up experiments conducted nine days after Kawahara (2026), which all failed to replicate this result. The most plausible explanation is an unannounced change in the safeguard mechanisms.

records.title: Animal Implicatures: A Note on the Informativity Principle and Bayesianism
records.abstract: Several recent analyses of animal signals have proposed that when animals have the choice between a signal S and a more informative signal S+, S+ is preferred if it is true (= Informativity Principle). The principle is usually taken to apply both in production and in comprehension. A Gricean analysis currently lacks plausibility for lack of evidence for a theory of mind in the target species. But this doesn’t mean that the animal Informativity Principle must be entirely taken as primitive. In fact, some uses of the principle in comprehension can be replaced with simple Bayesian reasoning. We explain in which cases this happens, and why the key data adduced for the Informativity Principle cannot be explained in this way because they involve production rather than comprehension. This suggests a new division of labor in which the animal Informativity Principle is primitive in production, but derived from Bayesian reasoning in comprehension.

records.title: Is it syntax or syncretism? Phases and honorific case markers in Korean
records.abstract: This work develops a phase-based analysis of Korean honorific case markers. Korean displays an asymmetry in its case paradigm: while nominative, dative, and vocative case markers have their honorific counterparts, the accusative case marker does not. I argue that this gap is not accidental. Instead, it follows from phasehood in syntax. Adopting the view that vP, ApplP, and CP are phases (Chomsky 2000; 2001; McGinnis 2000; Ershova 2024), I propose that an honorific head (H) selects a phase and establishes agreement with the closest [+HUMAN] argument at the phase edge. This work demonstrates that syntax, rather than morphological syncretism, offers an explanation for the empirical puzzle at issue.

records.title: The Morphosyntactic–Semantic Unity of the Early Middle Japanese Realis Form Izenkei: the -ru ≈ -re allomorphy and the so-called kakari-musubi
records.abstract: This study proposes a unified morphosyntactic–semantic account of the suffixal form -re found in the EMJ realis paradigm — the so-called izenkei — and related phenomena. It argues that -re is a contextual allomorph of the inflexional suffix -ru, which marks a clause as [0PAST, +ACTUAL-WORLD-COMMITMENT] and thereby presents the eventuality expressed by that clause as belonging to the actual world lato sensu. It surfaces as -re when the clause is set as a premise. This premise-setting environment is supplied overtly by the suffixes -ba [+CONDITIONAL] and -do(mo) [+CONCESSIVE], and covertly by the phonologically null suffix -Ø [+PREM(ISE-SETTING)] in the =koso type of kakari-musubi. Thus, the focus particle =koso does not itself condition the allomorphy -ru → -re, but merely focalises a constituent not containing the finite predicate within a clause already set as a premise by -Ø [+PREM]. In the =zo/=namu type, by contrast, a clause with a topic–comment articulation is first constructed, and its topic constituent containing the finite predicate is nominalised by -Ø [+NOM(INAL)] so that it can be treated as a topic NP. The focus particle =zo or =namu is then added to the comment. The resulting construction is analysed as a COPULA-LESS INVERTED PSEUDO-CLEFT in which the comment/focus precedes the nominalised topic/background without the intervention of the pseudo-copula =n-ari. This pseudo-cleft has two further types: the =ka type and the =ya type. The distribution of the focus particles is simple: in an interrogative clause, =ka is selected if an interrogative phrase constitutes the focus, whereas =ya is selected if a non-interrogative phrase constitutes the focus; in a declarative clause, =zo/=namu is selected. Cross-linguistically, Spanish and Portuguese provide close structural parallels to the =zo/=namu, =ya and =ka types. The =koso type, by contrast, contains no such nominalised topic phrase containing a finite predicate and is therefore NOT a PSEUDO-CLEFT. NOR does there seem to be any syntactic evidence that it is an IT-CLEFT. Finally, the absence of a special predicate form with the focus particles =ha and =mo follows from the set-based nature of their focalisation, which presupposes a contextually relevant set rather than a clause set as a premise by -Ø [+PREM]. Furthermore, in these constructions, no constituent containing a finite predicate constitutes the topic, and hence no such constituent is nominalised by -Ø [+NOM] to form a topic NP. Accordingly, the particles themselves do not determine the predicate forms. Rather, the configuration is constructed FIRST and only THEN determines both the predicate form and which focus particle may occur. Traditional particle–predicate concord called kakari-musubi is therefore reanalysed as a surface correspondence between two consequences of the same independently constructed structure.

records.title: Varieties of headless relative clauses in Tigrinya
records.abstract: This paper presents the first systematic description of headless relative clauses in Tigrinya (Semitic; Eritrea and Ethiopia; SOV).
